key_insight: Universal Textual Teaching (UTT) turns teacher-student knowledge gaps into a reusable natural-language "Primer," avoiding parameter updates while still improving LLM reasoning and code performance.
engineering_relevance: UTT offers a practical distillation route for API-only or expensive-to-train models because the learned teaching signal is stored as text rather than tied to a specific architecture.
method: Select representative teacher-student gap cases via paired evaluation.

Iteratively refine a Primer through multi-role interaction: Student attempts, Prompter converts feedback into instruction, Teacher gives a targeted demo, and Synthesizer consolidates validated lessons.
Reuse the final Primer across different students and teacher-student pairs.
evidence_signal: On Omni-MATH-2 and KernelBench, the abstract reports large gains, including math accuracy rising from 27.6% to 51.7% and KernelBench accuracy from 9.4% to 48.6% (Fast1: 9% to 35%), outperforming prompt-engineering and parameter-based KD baselines.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on identifying representative gap cases and iterative multi-role prompting, performance may be sensitive to prompt design, evaluation quality, and transfer to very different model families.
